newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 4.

text.p: Wild horse auction successful: Conservation Minister Nick Smith said on Sunday he was rapt that almost all the Kaimanawa wild horses offered for auction at the weekend were sold, saving them from the abattoir. Page 1.

Bolger keen to retain power: Prime Minister Jim Bolger renewed at the weekend his vow to lead National into the next election -- but many delegates at the party's annual conference said privately that they wanted him to quit next year. Page 2.

Farmers plead for help: Farmers pleaded for help from the government at the National Party's conference at the weekend, saying rural New Zealand was dying and the party itself was under threat. Page 2.
Data tipped to show jobless rise: Survey results due out tomorrow were expected to show unemployment was on the rise and employment levels were in decline, economists said. Page 13.
Lithium processor looks to Japan's demand: Auckland-based Pacific Lithium expects to supply up to half the Japanese demand for the raw product in lithium batteries this year. Page 13.

DML left with lease costs for idle contracting plant: Contract mining business lost by Skellerup Group offshoot DML Contracting has left the company paying lease costs of several million dollars for idle equipment. Page 13.

THL predicts $6m drop in profits: Tourism Holdings, formerly the Helicopter Line, is forecasting a profit of about $6 million for the year to June, less than half of last year's $12.2 million. Page 13.

Chilly blast shuts down Winter Carnival: Christchurch's Winter Carnival was one of the casualties of the weekend's wintry blast which forced that cancellation of many weekend sports and leisure activities.

Papers cast doubts on Kirton view: Confidential papers show the Associate Minister of Health, Neil Kirton, did not tell Parliament the full story over a government advertising contract which went to a firm headed by his brother-in-law.

Maine salvage may be too little for bonds: Goldman Sachs' $40 million salvage package of Maine Investments is estimated to be worth as little as $10 million in immediate benefit to the bond holders who helped to finance Maine's buyout of Skellerup Group.

Telecoms users call for help: The government should intervene more to help resolve disputes between telecommunications companies, say nearly half the senior executives in the latest Business Herald/University of Auckland survey.
Costs see NZ miss out: Foreign investment managers offering products locally may bypass New Zealand because of the removal of an exemption from disclosure requirements under the Securities Act.
IES looking to expand in NZ: United States electricity company IES Industries is looking to expand its operations in New Zealand, especially in the power generation sector.

Singapore hails Air NZ alliance: After a half a century in the skies, Singapore Airlines is hailing its alliance with Air New Zealand as a chance to lure more passengers and cut costs in an increasingly competitive market.
